instructions: Start the rice first. Rinse 1 1/2 cups rice and cook it by the directions on the package.
Cut the mushrooms in half, or in quarters if they're large. Thinly slice the shallots. Smash the ginger with the flat of a knife and break it into small pieces.
In a large bowl, toss the mushrooms with the soy sauce, pepper, bouillon powder, ginger and half of the shallots. Leave them for 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Add the rest of the shallots and cook for 1 minute, until they smell fragrant.
Add the mushrooms with everything left in the bowl, and the sugar. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until they start to brown and shrink.
Add 1 1/2 cups water and bring it to a boil over medium-high.
Turn the heat to medium-low and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes, until the sauce is thick and glossy and the mushrooms are tender.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a splash of soy sauce.
method_notes: Mai and Maxime's version leads: mushrooms marinated for 15 minutes in soy, pepper, bouillon, ginger and shallot, browned in oil, then simmered in water until the sauce reduces. The amounts are doubled for four, with cremini in place of straw and chestnut mushrooms and a spoonful of plain sugar instead of the caramel nuoc hang. Vegan Vietnamese and Full of Plants cook mushrooms with tofu and a coconut-soda sauce, which is a different dish, so they only shaped the rice-first timing. The pepper is the main flavor; use 1 tsp if you want it gentler. No version showed ratings.
